nodes.content: Design a distributed join executor that adapts to changing key skew while preserving bounded memory and retry-safe output.
requirements: Preserve SQL bag semantics under worker retries while respecting a 512 MiB per-worker memory cap.
Reduce p95 completion time 30% versus static hash partitioning on shifting-skew workloads with equal resources.

nodes.content: Use barrier-synchronized hot-key splitting with small-side replication, 384-MiB spill-triggered joins, and atomic output commits keyed by input-row-ID pairs.
How should split fanout and replication strategy change when both sides of a hot key exceed the 384-MiB spill threshold?
Adaptive 2D grid fanout with spill-backed replication keeps dual-large hot-key RSS ≤512 MiB and lowers shifting-skew p95 ≥30%.
Benchmark dual-large-key ShiftSkew-10M under injected retries against equal-resource static hashing; measure p95, peak RSS, and bag-count errors.
On ShiftSkew-10M with retries, adaptive grid cut p95 34% versus static hashing; peak RSS was 498 MiB, bag-count errors zero.
Adopt adaptive 2D grid fanout for dual-large keys because ShiftSkew-10M met p95, RSS, and retry-safe bag-count targets.
Implement adopted 2D grid: size fanout from barrier samples for ≤384-MiB task memory, spill replicas, atomically commit row-pair outputs.
Implement GridRouter v1: compute fanout from barrier samples, spill replicas above 384 MiB, and atomically commit row-pair output manifests.
GridRouter v1 delivers barrier-sampled 2D routing, 384-MiB spill-backed replicas, and attempt-fenced atomic manifests for unique input-row-pair outputs.
Test GridRouter v1 on ShiftSkew-10M with crash-retries; compare bag multiplicities, peak RSS, and p95 against static hashing.
On ShiftSkew-10M, GridRouter v1 cut p95 33% versus static hashing; peak RSS was 501 MiB, with zero crash-retry bag-multiplicity mismatches.
Run BagRetry-1M with duplicate keys, NULLs, barrier-time worker crashes, and spill pressure; audit SQL multiplicities and peak RSS.
BagRetry-1M found 41 missing matches after barrier retries: epoch-local row-ID collisions suppressed distinct bag outputs; peak RSS was 503 MiB.
Retain adaptive routing's 33% p95 gain, but block release until stable source/split/offset IDs fix 41 retry-missing matches.
Update GridRouter to derive 2D fanout from both-side byte estimates, spill replicas, and fence commits by paired stable source/split/offset IDs.
Patch GridRouter v2 to persist source/split/offset IDs across epochs and atomically commit paired-ID manifests under attempt fencing.
GridRouter v2 replaces epoch-local row IDs with persisted source/split/offset pairs in attempt-fenced atomic output manifests.
Rerun BagRetry-1M and ShiftSkew-10M on GridRouter v2 with barrier crashes; verify multiplicities, peak RSS, and equal-resource p95.
GridRouter v2: BagRetry-1M had zero multiplicity errors; ShiftSkew-10M p95 fell 32% versus static hashing; peak RSS 506 MiB.
Schedule sampled hot-key sort-merge tiles via work stealing; spill above 384 MiB and commit each deterministic tile once.
What sort-merge tile size minimizes spill I/O and stealing overhead when hot keys shift mid-epoch?
64-MiB tiles minimize combined spill bytes and steal overhead versus 32/128-MiB tiles on ShiftSkew-10M.
Benchmark 32/64/128-MiB tiles on retry-injected ShiftSkew-10M against static hashing; measure spill I/O, steal overhead, p95, RSS, multiplicities.
ShiftSkew-10M: 64-MiB tiles cut spill-plus-steal time 18% versus alternatives; p95 31% below static, RSS 496 MiB, zero multiplicity errors.
Stress 64-MiB sort-merge tiles on DupBurst-5M with million-row duplicate runs and stolen-task crashes; audit p95, RSS, multiplicities.
DupBurst-5M duplicate runs drove sort-merge RSS to 579 MiB despite spilling, violating the 512-MiB cap.
Defer 64-MiB sort-merge tiles despite 31% p95 gain; DupBurst-5M exceeded the memory cap at 579 MiB.
Can disk-backed duplicate-run iterators keep sort-merge RSS below 512 MiB without losing its 30% p95 gain?
Disk-backed duplicate-run iterators will cap DupBurst-5M RSS below 512 MiB while retaining ≥30% ShiftSkew-10M p95 improvement.
Prototype disk-backed duplicate-run iterators for deferred 64-MiB tiles; rerun DupBurst-5M and ShiftSkew-10M, measuring RSS, p95, and multiplicities.
With disk-backed runs, DupBurst-5M peak RSS was 487 MiB; ShiftSkew-10M p95 fell 30.5% versus static; multiplicity errors zero.
Stress deferred disk-backed 64-MiB tiles on SkewBurst-10M with shifting duplicate keys and crashes; compare static-hash p95, RSS, multiplicities.
SkewBurst-10M comparison exposed unequal shuffle slots in n29; correcting them reduced ShiftSkew-10M’s equal-resource p95 gain to 27%.
Keep sort-merge tiles deferred: disk-backed runs satisfy memory, but corrected equal-resource p95 improvement is 27%, below target.
Optimize deferred disk-backed tiles with 8-MiB asynchronous prefetch, then retest equal-slot p95 and RSS on both skew workloads.
Implement 8-MiB asynchronous prefetch for disk-backed duplicate-run iterators, accounting buffers within the 384-MiB spill budget.
TileMerge v2 adds budget-accounted 8-MiB asynchronous prefetch to disk-backed duplicate-run iterators, retaining deterministic tile commit IDs.
Benchmark TileMerge v2 on ShiftSkew-10M and SkewBurst-10M with equal shuffle slots and retries; measure p95, RSS, multiplicities.
TileMerge v2 achieved equal-slot p95 gains of 31% on ShiftSkew-10M and 30% on SkewBurst-10M; RSS ≤499 MiB, zero multiplicity errors.
Adopt TileMerge v2 over deferred tiles: equal-slot p95 gains reach ≥30%, RSS ≤499 MiB, and retry multiplicities match.
Use live hot-key microshard migration with small-side replication, 384-MiB spill thresholds, and attempt-fenced stable row-pair commits.
How can in-flight microshards migrate without losing or duplicating join pairs when retries cross routing-version changes?
Version-fenced handoffs and stable source/split/offset pair IDs yield zero missing or duplicate matches across mid-epoch migrations with crashes.
Prototype version-fenced handoffs; test MidEpoch-5M with migration-time crashes, auditing bag counts, peak RSS, and equal-resource p95.
MidEpoch-5M migration crashes yielded zero missing or duplicate pairs; peak RSS 504 MiB, equal-slot p95 35% below static hashing.
Stress live migration on FanoutFlip-10M with alternating hot keys and dual-large join sides; check pair multiplicities, RSS, equal-slot p95.
FanoutFlip-10M dual-large keys made small-side replication unavailable; migrating buffered shards peaked at 548 MiB, exceeding the cap.
Defer live migration despite MidEpoch-5M's 35% p95 gain; dual-large FanoutFlip-10M breached memory at 548 MiB.
Can spill-backed handoff eliminate duplicate migration buffers for dual-large keys while keeping FanoutFlip-10M RSS below 512 MiB?
Spill-backed handoff with 32-MiB transfer windows keeps FanoutFlip-10M peak RSS ≤512 MiB without reducing p95 gain below 30%.
Prototype spill-backed 32-MiB handoff windows for deferred migration; rerun FanoutFlip-10M measuring peak RSS, equal-slot p95, and bag multiplicities.
Spill-backed handoffs on FanoutFlip-10M peaked at 492 MiB; equal-slot p95 fell 32% versus static, with zero multiplicity mismatches.
Resume live migration only with spill-backed handoffs: FanoutFlip-10M recovered cap compliance and 32% p95 gain without bag errors.
Implement version-fenced 32-MiB spill-backed handoffs, reserve transfer buffers within 384 MiB, and verify migration crashes on FanoutFlip-10M.
Implement LiveShard v2 handoff: spill sender buffers, transfer 32-MiB windows, fence routing versions, and reserve window memory.
LiveShard v2 adds spill-backed 32-MiB migration windows, version-fenced handoffs, budgeted transfer buffers, and stable-pair output manifests.
Crash senders and receivers mid-handoff on FanoutFlip-10M; audit LiveShard v2 bag multiplicities, peak RSS, and equal-slot p95.
LiveShard v2 FanoutFlip-10M handoff crashes produced zero bag mismatches; peak RSS 501 MiB, equal-slot p95 31% below static.
Ship GridRouter v2 by default; use TileMerge v2 for duplicate runs and spill-backed LiveShard v2 for shifting dual-large keys.
